07:17 PM EDT
Busy schedule this weekend for the candidates
Friday will see former President Donald Trump addressing the Fraternal Order of Police in Charlotte, North Carolina at the University City Hilton. The order's president, Patrick Yoes, said Trump "led our nation admirably through some very tough times."
Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff will be in Chicago for his second day of delivering remarks at a campaign reception. He was in Los Angeles today.
On Saturday, Trump will hold a rally in Mosinee, Wisconsin at 2 p.m.
Gov. Tim Walz will deliver a keynote remark at the Human Rights Campaign, the nation's largest LGBTQ+ civil rights organization, annual national dinner on Saturday.
The organization recently endorsed the Harris-Walz ticket. Walz served as a faculty sponsor while he was a teacher for his school's first gay-straight alliance. As Governor, he he enacted policies to ban conversion therapy and protect access to health care for LGBTQ+ people in Minnesota.
--Monica Sager
07:15 PM EDT
Vance urges voters to cast those ballots
Vance ended his rally by asking supporters to "get out there and vote 10 times" adding that he did not mean voter fraud, but for those supporters to take nine others with them to the polls.
"We're going to give this country an president it deserves," he said.
-- Dan Gooding
07:07 PM EDT
Vance responds to question about Georgia high shooting
Asked about Wednesday's shooting in Georgia, Vance says school shootings happen in states with and without strict gun laws, claiming this showed extra laws were not the answer.
To solve the problem, Vance said school security needed to be increased to prevent "psychos" from carrying out further shootings.
-- Dan Gooding
07:05 PM EDT
Vance on McCain's son: 'Who cares what somebody's family thinks'
Vance was asked about the late John McCain's son endorsing Kamala Harris and said he knew that the 2008 Republican presidential candidate did not let personal disagreements get in the way of serving the country.
Vance said that he did not believe for a second that McCain would have supported Kamala Harris because of issues at the U.S.-Mexico border.
"Who cares what somebody's family thinks about the presidential race?" Vance said, before gesturing at the audience. "I care about what these people care about the presidential race.
He then countered his point, saying: "I don't know if anybody noticed, but pretty much every single member of Tim Walz's family came out and endorsed Donald Trump. Is that a bigger story than what John McCain's son said? I think so."
-- Dan Gooding
07:02 PM EDT
Walz ends speech with a 'pep talk'
Walz finished his speech in Erie as always in Coach-fashion with a "pep talk because we're about at kick-off time here."
"Pennsylvania and Minnesota have a lot in common. We have a lot of beautiful lakes. We get a lot of snow. Super Bowl rings we do not have in common, but we will get one some day," Walz said. "But we share a history. It was our people that built this country. It was the miners of the Iron Range of Minnesota who pulled that taconite from under the ground that fueled the gas furnaces of the steel mills that built the steel that built the tanks that liberated Europe from Nazi tyranny. That was our people."
Walz talked about how both Pennsylvanians and Minnesotans are optimistic
"For Christ's sake, you get 10 feet of snow here and you just plow it and smile. That's what you do," Walz said. "It's about pushing back the pessimism and pushing forward the optimism. Here's our deal. We are in the big game, all of us fourth quarter. We're down a field goal. Clock is ticking. We're the underdogs at this point, but that's ok. Our people have always been the underdogs. Our people have always known how to do the work. Our people have always gone against the odds."
But Walz said the "ball's in our hands" and it is Erie's time to vote.
"Our job's to do the blocking and tackling of politics – an inch at a time, a yard at a time, phone call at a time, door knock at a time, $5 donation at a time, a rally at a time, whatever it takes," he said. "We're in the game. The momentum's behind us."
He said everyone throughout the country should care because "politics is into you." No matter if it's in Erie or somewhere else, Walz encouraged the attendees to "do the work" in the next 61 days.
"People are coming out across this country saying enough with the pessimism, enough with the shit talking in this country and let's find a new way forward," Walz said. "We believe in a hopeful future. We get to make this happen."
-- Monica Sager
06:55 PM EDT
Vance on voting rights
Vance was asked about voting rights and monitoring election day.
He said that Republicans have a bill in Congress which would ensure only U.S. citizens would be able to vote, despite that being the case at many levels of local, state and federal elections.
06:51 PM EDT
Vance: 'Every citizen controls his own destiny'
"In America, every citizen controls his own destiny, every woman controls her own future," Vance said, adding that Trump wanted to rebuild the American promise.
The GOP wants to stop sending money overseas to "tinpot dictators", Vance said, and end jobs heading abroad, also.
He also said Democrats had been raising taxes to give immigrants benefits while also sending that cash to other countries.
"Donald Trump says that is bogus, we're not doing that anymore," Vance said.
"If America first means anything, it means we're prioritizing the American worker, we're prioritizing the American citizen, and we are rebuilding a country where wherever you came from, whatever your background is, whoever your parents were, liberty and justice for all."
-- Dan Gooding
06:49 PM EDT
Walz tells the crowd to pull out their phones
Gov. Tim Walz asked the audience to pull their phones out and record a message to send to their "undecided" friends, laying out the tax cuts, unions, Social Security and Medicare.
"Kamala Harris is here to make sure you make the decisions in your life that's right for your life for the choices that you and your family make," Walz said.
"It's not about name calling. It's weird to be obsessed with people's personal lives. It's weird to be obsessed with people's health care choices. It's weird to continue to talk about sharks and batteries and boats and things like that. What's not weird is telling us what you're going to do about health care, tell us who's going to get a tax cut, tell us that you're going to protect reproductive rights, tell us how you're going to tackle climate change."
"You're going to decide the direction that we go in," Walz said. "This divisiveness, this anger, we get to decide that we're tired of it. I'm sick of it every day. Remember when you used to go weeks or months without talking about the damn president? Because people were doing their job. They were getting things done. That's the way we want to be."
-- Monica Sager
06:46 PM EDT
Vance takes swipe at Harris' campaign slogan
Donald Trump's Vice Presidential pick took a swipe at Harris' campaign slogan "We're not going back", asking "to what?"
"To low inflation? Rising take home pay? We're not going back to a secure Southern border?" Vance said.
He claimed Harris wanted to take the country back to a time when Americans needed to be rich to enjoy safety, to be able to buy a home and "enjoy a nice steak on a Friday night".
-- Dan Gooding
06:45 PM EDT
Vance talks about his mom's struggle with drug addiction
Vance one again spoke of his mother's struggle with opioid addiction during his childhood, after starting to say she was addicted to fentanyl and then correcting himself.
The senator said fentanyl was coming across the southwest border, smuggled by immigrants, and once more placed the blame on Harris for this problem.
He spoke of drug cartels hiding the lethal drug in bags of candy and that this was going to cost children their lives.
"Our children's leadership has failed them," Vance said. "What kind of a person lets drug cartels do business in their country? What kind of a person allows the drug cartels to disguise fentanyl as candy? And what kind of a person invites these people to get rich of of this country while its own citizens die?
"I don't want to answer that question, but she sure as hell should not be President of the United States."
-- Dan Gooding
06:43 PM EDT
Walz talks about Georgia HS shooting: 'That community will never be the same'
Walz took a moment in his speech to talk about the school shooting that took place in Georgia yesterday.
"Kids were going to school, the first week of school, excited," Walz said. "Now we have four dead. Our hearts go out to the two students and the two teachers that were killed and their families being in mourning. There's many injured in Winder and that community will never be the same."
As a teacher and father, Walz said he loves back to school because of the hope and opportunity it brings.
"Now for those kids it will always be a time of sheer terror," Walz said. "That will be a memory that they'll hold forever. It's a reminder for the rest of the country that we have work to do. I for one am sick and tired of hearing about thoughts and prayers rather than actually doing something."
-- Monica Sager
06:41 PM EDT
Vance and Trump united on 'common sense'
The Ohio senator said he and Trump were united on "common sense" policies around tackling immigration, as well as bringing down the cost of housing and groceries.
"And we're going to fire that crazy person Kamala Harris, we're not going to give her a promotion," Vance added.
-- Dan Gooding
06:39 PM EDT
Walz talks economics
Gov. Tim Walz is reiterating Vice President Kamala Harris' economic plan, which is met with loud applause and shouts of "ya."
"Every single community in this country matters," Walz said.
"When you grow up in a town like this or a town like Butte, Nebraska, you learn to take care of your neighbors...We have a saying where when we each do better, we all do better," Walz said.
The Democratic vice presidential candidate spoke of his hometown and how the people in his class did not grow up to be venture capitalists. They became nurses and firefighters or teachers.
"Those are the folks that need to get a tax cut. Those are the folks who need to get a break."
"He installed three Supreme Court Justices who took away our right to control our own bodies," Walz said about Trump. "He did all of that before he tried to violently overthrow our democratic government by the way, in an election that he got his butt whipped fair and square and lost. It's that simple."
"He openly says these things that we need to talk to our relatives about," Walz said. "And we all know I need to talk to my relatives too. Trust me on this. Nothing makes you more Midwestern than having your family be on this stuff."
"They're talking about cutting Social Security and Medicare, repealing the Affordable Care Act and protections like this," Walz said. "If you're a billionaire, you don't give a damn about Social Security and Medicare. If you're my mom who has to pay her heat bill and her food with it, it matters a lot. The vast majority of people care about this."
"If I were him, I'd be hiding down in Mar-a-Lago too. I wouldn't want to face working people," Walz said. "I wouldn't want to look them in the eye and tell them why their work doesn't matter, why it should be harder for them to unionize, why he and his folks have undermined middle America."
Walz mentioned is Republican opponent Vance, saying that the Senator says he's a part of middle America. Vance says there's "a lot of angst" there, which Walz said is because of him and others who have "gutted Middle America."
"You go off to Yale, you get a philosophy major. You write a best-selling book, trash the very people you grow up with, just don't come back to Erie and tell us how to run our lives," Walz said.
"I don't think it inspires people to run against something, but I do think it's important to remind people are because they're going to try to slip out of it every step of the way," Walz said. "We need to be clear what we stand for. When Kamala Harris talks about freedom, she believes you should be free to make your own health care decisions. Simple as that. We believe education should be a ticket to the middle class, not a ticket to crippling debt. We believe we should have the freedom to drink clean water and breathe clean air. And yeah, we believe in the freedom to send our kids to school without being shot dead in the hall."
-- Monica Sager
06:33 PM EDT
Vance: 'Going to reimplement deportations in this country'
Vance said Harris supported open border policies and allowed migrants to access free healthcare and other benefits. He promised Donald Trump would reverse these policies and continue building the border wall with Mexico.
"Here's what we're going to do on top of it: we're going to reimplement deportations in this country," Vance said, despite record deportations recently under President Biden.
The Ohio senator said he and Trump were united on "common sense" policies around tackling immigration, as well as bringing down the cost of housing and groceries.
"And we're going to fire that crazy person Kamala Harris, we're not going to give her a promotion," Vance added.
-- Dan Gooding
06:22 PM EDT
Tim Walz: 'This is hopeful'
The Democratic vice-presidential nominee said that his opponents, former President Donald Trump and Sen. JD Vance, are trying to convince voters that the election is something made out of fear, that it is a bad thing.
"We've got work to do this fall," Walz said. "This is a joyful thing we're doing. This is hopeful."
Walz said Harris is running on a plan "where everybody belongs and everybody can get ahead."
Walz shared moments from Savannah, Georgia where it was just him, Harris, and their partners. There were former President Donald Trump supporters present, but that didn't fluster the Vice President.
"She never missed a beat. She turned around and looked at me and she said 'Don't ever forget. We work as hard for them and their family and for the things that are right for them as we do for this side," Walz said. "She's talking about those folks because we're trying to get them because our policies will make their lives better."
-- Monica Sager
06:20 PM EDT
Vance promises to talk border
Vance is promising to talk about the southwest border, saying Arizonans see the effects of the current administration's policies firsthand. He then said he would take questions from the media, adding that they would likely not be friendly but it was important to speak to them anyway.
"This campaign, my friends, is about a very simple thing: it's about taking this country back and taking the great Arizona leadership style to Washington D.C.," Vance continued. "There's no way to do that unless we fire San Francisco liberal Kamala Harris and promote Donald Trump to President of the United States."
-- Dan Gooding
06:19 PM EDT
Tim Walz: 'Coach signs warm my heart'
Tim Walz said he met a 94-year-old in the crowd who taught for 45 years. She is at the rally because she believes in the "way forward," the Governor said.
"The coach signs warm my heart. Thank you," Walz said. "That state championship is as fresh today as it was 25 years ago."
Walz said the first days of school shows that there is an "opportunity to build something better," that "anything is possible."
-- Monica Sager
06:18 PM EDT
JD Vance takes the stage in Arizona
Ohio Senator JD Vance took to the stage in Arizona, surrounded by Trump Vance signs.
"I've been in politics for all of two years and you meet some really good people and you meet some real scumbags," Vance began, to a slight pause from the crowd. "You in Arizona, you have some of the best people representing the state of Arizona."
Shouts of "JD" then rang out from supporters.
-- Dan Gooding
06:14 PM EDT
Tim Walz starts with jokes
Gov. Tim Walz takes the stage in Erie, Pennsylvania. Attendees are holding "Kamala" and "Coach" signs and shouting "Gov, Gov, Gov."
"Thank you, Erie," Walz said. "Erie, you might know, a while back Donald Trump said these crowds are all AI. You know what's not AI? Your votes."
-- Monica Sager

Tim Walz greets Erie
I’m in Erie, Pennsylvania to talk about how we’re going to win the fight for our freedoms, our families, and our future.
Tune in.

05:53 PM EDT
Newsmax Guest Supports Kamala Harris
Ryan Yonk, with the American Institute for Economic Research, said on Newsmax that Vice President Kamala Harris's proposal for a $50,000 tax cut for small businesses is a good idea.
"A tax cut like this that would encourage business growth is always a better option that trying to direct where it should go," Yonk said.
Harris announced her economic plan in New Hampshire to expand tax incentives for small businesses, calling it an "opportunity economy."
As part of it, she laid out a way to break the financial barrier for entrepreneurs, by raising the tax deduction from $5,000 to $50,000.
-- Monica Sager
05:52 PM EDT
Harris' Big Weekend Plans
Ahead of the presidential debate on Tuesday, the Vice President Kamala Harris and Gov. Tim Walz campaign are announcing a "historic Weekend of Action to underscore the dangers of Trump's Project 2025 with battleground voters."
This will be the campaign's largest Weekend of Action to date, with over 20,000 volunteer shifts and over 2,000 events to reach more than 1 million voters.
"With hundreds of offices and thousands of staff across the battlegrounds, we are able to harness all the buzz around the debate and break through to hard-to-reach voters on Project 2025," said Dan Kanninen, battleground states director for Harris-Walz. "We are speaking to those Americans who are turned off by Trump's extremism and making sure they know there's a home for them in Vice President Harris' campaign."
Sen. Amy Klobuchar, Jon Ossoff and Alex Padilla as well as The Honorable Miguel Cardona will host events throughout the weekend. Celebrities are expected to help as well, including Bill Nye, actor Wendell Pierce and TV personality Shereé Whitfield.
In addition to canvass launches, phone banks and cookouts, the campaign will host Project 2025 message trainings virtually and in-person in the battleground states. To date, the campaign has already held over 60 of these trainings.
Kanninen said the new support from Rep. Liz Cheney and First Lt. Jimmy McCain was "a powerful signal to swing voters."
This weekend, we are building on that momentum and taking our message directly to the voters who will decide this election in our largest ever campaign mobilization," Kanninen said.
-- Monica Sager
05:44 PM EDT
Trump's Abortion Issue
Joseph Weber, former professor and journalist, wrote for The Big Picture newsletter that former President Donald Trump has a problem with the large turnout the overturn of Roe v. Wade has lit for Democratic voters.
Weber noted that Harris' bus tour for reproductive freedom is a defense against Trump, and the Republican nominee is "struggling to message on an issue that is rising in importance heading into November."
-- Monica Sager
05:19 PM EDT
JD Vance Captured Being Mr. Dad
Ahead of his speech in Phoenix, Sen. JD Vance posted to X, formerly known as Twitter, a photo of him carrying his children walking around Scottsdale.
"After 20 minutes in the Arizona heat the Vance kids were done," he posted.

Teamsters Union to Meet with Kamala Harris
Teamsters Union is to meet with Vice President Kamala Harris on Sept. 16 in Washington D.C. at the Union's headquarters.
The union, which represents over one million workers across industries, has yet to endorse a candidate. They held a roundtable with Trump already.
"We look forward to having a conversation on the direction of the country and the issues that matter to working people," Teamsters President Sean O'Brien said.
04:57 PM EDT

Second Gentelman Doug Emhoff said there's "such a clear contrast" between his wife, Vice President Kamala Harris, and former President Donald Trump.
"Everyone's life would be remarkably worse if somehow this guy who's completely unfit for office ever returned," Emhoff said. "People would be so far worse off, including business folks."
Emhoff spoke in Los Angeles today.

Pete Buttigieg Raising Funds for Kamala Harris
Transportation Sec. Pete Buttigieg raised $4 million for Vice President Kamala Harris yesterday, as reported by Politico.
He held five fundraisers in Northern California in his own personal capacity.

04:40 PM EDT
Tim Walz Speaks in Pennsylvania Tonight
Gov. Tim Walz, Harris's running mate, will speak an hour later, at 6 p.m. in Erie, Pennsylvania. This will be his second day in the battleground state with other political events in Lancaster and Pittsburgh.
04:33 PM EDT
Swifties for Kamala Raise $122K With Merchandise Sales
Swifties for Kamala has announced that its "Voting Era" merch collection has raised $13,000 for "organizations working to register voters and help them have their voices heard and elect Democratic leaders up-and-down the ballot who will protect our democracy and rights."
The group announced the merch drop on Aug. 27 during its Zoom webinar kickoff call. Over 20,000 Swifties were on the call to hear from big-name Taylor Swift-fans like Representatives Becca Balint and Chris Deluzio, Senators
Kirsten Gillibrand
,
Ed Markey
,
Elizabeth Warren
, and Carole King.
On that night, the group raised over $122,000.
-- Monica Sager
04:24 PM EDT
New Hampshire Gov. Chris Sununu calls out Harris
New Hampshire Gov. Chris Sununu said Vice President Kamala Harris' economic plan, which she announced yesterday in his state, is actually "playing into the hands" of large businesses.
"I don't think she understands a lot of this when it comes to the economy, how things work," Sununu said. "When she came out and said price controls, that scared everybody."
Sununu called Harris' plan moderate, but "she can't get away" from the inflation she has "been there" for that has "crushed families." Sununu is predicting that former President Donald Trump wins New Hampshire by a few percentage points.
"The honeymoon is over," Sununu said. "People are demanding accountability."
-- Monica Sager
04:16 PM EDT
JD Vance Set to Speak in Arizona
Sen. JD Vance, the Republican vice-presidential nominee, will deliver remarks in Phoenix, Arizona at 6 p.m. EST. The campaign's press release indicated Vance will discuss "migrant crime and the flow of deadly drugs."
04:07 PM EDT
Harris' response to Trump's idea to lift sanctions
In response to Former President Donald Trump suggesting he will "use sanctions as little as possible" during a speech in New York today, Vice President Kamala Harris's campaign retorted that the Biden-Harris Administration has imposed over 600 new sanctions on Iran and "its destabilizing terrorist proxies like Hamas and Hezbollah."
"Unilaterally lifting sanctions on Iran and Russia is the exact kind of reckless foreign policy we've come to expect from Donald Trump, who would make America weak and the world less safe. As president, he emboldened North Korea, Iran, and Russia," said Morgan Finklestein, national security spokesperson for Harris-Walz 2024.
"If Trump returns to office, he will undermine our security, turn his back on our allies and have America go it alone, strengthen our adversaries, and disrespect the title of commander-in-chief."
Harris has been a "critical leader" to rally the word for economic pressure on Russia. Trump, however, has "cozy up" to the dictators, the campaign said.
"Even his own former national security advisors have warned of the danger that Trump represents for America and the world," Finklestein said. "There is one candidate in this race who has the strength and resolve to stand up for America, our service members, and our allies, and defend democracy at home and abroad."

Team Harris-Walz Launches Second Ad
Today,
Team Harris-Walz
launched its second ad in its media blitz against
Project 2025
.
The ad highlights the "dangers of Trump's extreme agenda." The television showing, which is called "Backwards," is meant to show the "devastating impact" Trump's plans would have on Black Americans.
"
Donald Trump's
Project 2025 makes one thing clear to Black America: he doesn't give a damn about us," said Quentin Fulks, principal duty campaign manager for Harris-Walz. "His Project 2025 will take our community backwards; ripping away voting rights protections, reproductive freedom, eliminate the Department of Education, and require states to monitor pregnancies."
"Backwards" is part of the Vice President and Governor's $370 million in digital and television advertising between Labor Day and Election Day.
The ad will air during sporting events in battleground states including Michigan vs. Texas on Sept. 7, Falcons vs. Steelers in NFL season opener on Sept. 8, Major League Baseball primetime and more.
It will also air during popular daytime television programming that over-indexes on Black Americans including
